clue.text: Unruly club maybe that gives outsider a chance to play

definitions.text: gives outsider a chance to play
definitions.note: the definition is a relative clause hanging off 'that': the thing that gives an outsider a chance to play

parts.note: a club is one suit of playing card; 'maybe' flags the example

explanation.surface: A rowdy sports club lets an outsider into the side.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'club' a team, but it is the card suit. A wild card is an entrant let into a tournament without qualifying.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild card is a place given to a player who has not qualified, letting an outsider play.

clue.text: Source of oil? Fancy!

definitions.meaning: a shaft drilled into the ground that oil is pumped up from
an old exclamation of mild surprise, as in 'Fancy that!'

explanation.surface: Someone learns where oil comes from and is duly amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy!' is the exclamation, not the adjective; 'Well!' does the same job, and an oil well is the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is drawn up from a well, and 'Well!' is said in surprise just as 'Fancy!' is.

clue.text: The French politician, source of illumination

explanation.surface: A French politician is hailed as a source of enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants a brilliant French statesman; 'illumination' is literal light.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain paraphrase: illumination is light, and a lamp is where a room's light comes from.

clue.text: Can new lead support item of lighting equipment?

indicators.note: a new version of the word lead has its letters freshly arranged

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A question whether a fresh piece of lead could hold up a light fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb opening a question, but it is the first piece of the answer; 'new' rearranges LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A candelabra is a branched holder for several candles, a piece of lighting equipment.

clue.text: Something to eat waiter finally put on a plate

indicators.note: in this down entry the single letter is placed on top of the rest
only the last letter of waiter is used

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken
a dish is a plate for serving food

explanation.surface: A waiter's last task is to put a snack onto a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a restaurant scene, but 'put on' is a positional signal for a down clue: the waiter's last letter sits above A DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crisp root vegetable eaten raw in salads, so it is something to eat.

clue.text: Electrical units in Hampshire

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the next word

explanation.surface: A note that some electrical units are found in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is an English county on the south coast; its name holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amps (amperes) are units of electric current.

clue.text: Paul came out to make confession of guilt

indicators.note: the letters come out of their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paul stepped forward to own up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came out' reads as stepping out or declaring oneself; 'out' alone is the rearranging instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Mea culpa is Latin for 'my fault', an admission of guilt.

clue.text: Normal flag

definitions.meaning: a banner carried on a pole, as by a regiment

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings; 'flag' could also be a verb (tire), but it is the banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means ordinary, and a standard is also a military or royal flag.

clue.text: Something published in Paris about a fizzy drink

indicators.note: LE MONDE goes round, about, the A

parts.note: Le Monde, the Paris daily newspaper
taken as it stands, and goes inside after the N

explanation.surface: A Paris publication runs a piece about a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the subject of'; it is the containment, with Le Monde wrapped round A.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain lemonade usually means a clear fizzy lemon drink, which is why 'fizzy' is enough.

clue.text: A form of domestic fuel coming back? It's a long story

parts.note: household gas, one kind of fuel

explanation.surface: Someone complains that getting the gas supply reconnected is a long story.
explanation.walkthrough: A + GAS reads AGAS, which then runs backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long, often rambling, narrative.

clue.text: Nanna, silly person joining artist for sung entertainment

explanation.surface: Granny and a fool team up with a painter to put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces simply follow one another; 'joining' strings them together.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand opera is serious opera sung throughout, with no spoken dialogue.

clue.text: Circulates and buys drinks for the group

definitions.meaning: in a pub, one drink for everyone in the party is a 'round'

explanation.surface: A sociable type works the room at the pub and stands everyone a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters split two ways: GETS AROUND (circulates) and GETS A ROUND (of drinks). The printed enumeration (4,6) follows the first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To get around is to circulate; to get a round is to buy drinks for everyone in the party.

clue.text: Tree home daughter gets south of West Country river

parts.note: the Tamar divides Devon from Cornwall in south-west England

explanation.surface: A daughter finds a house down in the south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is England's south-west; the River Tamar forms the Devon–Cornwall border.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical tree grown for its tangy pods.

clue.text: Food item — rubbish served up until start of afternoon

explanation.surface: A grumble that the lunch was rubbish and not served until afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' looks like restaurant talk, but only 'up' matters: in a down clue it flips ROT to TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin Mexican flatbread.

clue.text: An old playboy, not English nerd

explanation.surface: A one-time ladies' man turns out to be a bit of a geek.
explanation.walkthrough: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket, and in British slang an obsessive enthusiast, the kind who wears one while trainspotting.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls an obsessive hobbyist an anorak, after the jackets worn by trainspotters.

clue.text: Person with gun runs after bird

parts.note: the snipe is a wading bird
r = runs, as on a cricket scoreboard

explanation.surface: A hunter chases a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs after' reads as chasing, but 'runs' is just R. The word for the gunman itself comes from shooting snipe, a hard bird to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman firing from cover.

clue.text: Way holy person catches plane?

parts.note: a plane is a kind of tree; the '?' flags the example. It goes between S and T

explanation.surface: A saint boards an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' is the aircraft in the surface but the tree in the wordplay, common in London streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a way is a road, as in names like Watling Way.

clue.text: Helping after late changes or single change

indicators.note: the helping comes after the rearranged letters
the word late changes, its letters moved into a new order

parts.note: a ration is a fixed portion or helping of food

explanation.surface: A note about food portions served after late changes to a single change of plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' opens the clue as if it were the definition, but it is the portion that follows the reworked LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration is one modification made to something, such as an adjustment to a garment.

clue.text: Think highly of judge

definitions.meaning: informal: to admire or value someone
the verb: to assess or grade

explanation.surface: Someone admires a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun after 'of', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal use, to rate someone is to think highly of them; to rate also means to assess.

clue.text: Tilts, dropping a glass

indicators.note: the letter is dropped, taken out of the word

parts.note: something that tilts leans to one side

explanation.surface: A tilted drinking glass falls and breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glass' suggests a tumbler, but it means an optical piece such as a magnifying glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens is a shaped piece of glass that focuses light, and glasses are lenses for the eyes.

clue.text: I had left office, finally out of work

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: only the last letter of office is used

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone recalls leaving the office for good and ending up unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a story of quitting a job, which is what the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean not working or unemployed, as in workers laid idle by a strike.

clue.text: Drink ale, swallowing very little before "Time!"

indicators.note: to swallow is to take something inside

parts.note: v = very, as a small abbreviation; it goes between BE and ER
an age = a long period of time

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a last drop of ale before the barman calls time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' could be the instruction in the surface, but it is the definition. "Time!" is the British pub landlord's call at closing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: beverage is the formal word for any drink, hot or cold.

clue.text: Depict result of match finishing without winner

definitions.meaning: to show in a picture, with pencil or pen

definitions.text: result of match finishing without winner
definitions.meaning: a game ending level, a tie

explanation.walkthrough: A long second definition follows a one-word first.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to depict, and a draw is a game that ends level.

clue.text: Pilots with a maiden aboard vessels

parts.note: a + m, where m = maiden, a cricket over with no runs scored; it goes after STE

explanation.surface: Ships' pilots take a young woman on board their boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilots' looks like a noun but is the verb steers. In cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamers are steamships, vessels driven by steam.
